social_circle.name: Susan Barron

demographics.occupation: Retired elementary school teacher (3rd grade, Fairview Elementary, ~30 years); now book-club regular and household co-manager
demographics.education: Bachelor's degree in elementary education (Oregon teaching credential)

background.how_they_met: Met at a church potluck in Fairview in 1982 through mutual friends connected to one of Hal Greer's other apprentices.
background.why_close: Married since June 16, 1984. Co-parents of Daniel and Rachel, co-owners of the paid-off Fairview home since 1988, co-decision-makers on every major life choice from the mortgage payoff to the AARP long-term-care policy. Susan is Michael's primary confidante, sounding board, travel planner, and the person who sits in the dark workshop with him when his mother's dementia worsens.

interests: cooking seasonal meals from the garden
phone calls with her sister Karen
personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Full sentences, proper punctuation, no emoji or only the occasional smiley. Practical reminders mixed with affectionate one-liners. Drops a teacher-ish 'sweetheart' or 'honey' freely. Uses iMessage on an iPhone; will sometimes send a photo of a pie or the rhubarb without comment.

shared_activities: Daily 6:30 AM breakfast together
Sunday 9:30 service at First UMC Fairview + lunch out
Thursday-evening voter-pamphlet review one week before ballots are due
Bend road trips every ~6 weeks to see Rachel and the grandkids
Planning the 2027 Bath/Cotswolds/York trip
Joint household budget reviews and meal planning
social_circle.communication_frequency: daily (multiple times a day when apart)
recent_text_topics: Picking up lisinopril refill at the Fred Meyer pharmacy and whether Dr. Holcomb's office sent the new RSV booking
Pricing spring 2027 flights to Heathrow and a question about whether Bath or York gets the longer stop
Mom (Marjorie)'s Tuesday visit — the staff at the Gresham facility flagged a new medication; Susan asking if Michael wants her to come along
Grocery list for the week (her morning kitchen shift) and a reminder to grab brown ale that's on sale
Liam's school play next Friday — coordinating whether they drive to Hillsboro Wednesday or Friday
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q5: 'Susan is at the center of everything. We've been married forty-two years this June.' Q84: 'Married. To Susan. Since June 16, 1984.' Q18: post-retirement kitchen-sharing protocol. Q44: 'Susan found me out there... She didn't try to fix it. She just sat with me.' Q108: 'Susan's pricing flights for next spring.'

social_circle.name: Ray Mendoza
social_circle.relationship: best friend (fellow former Hal Greer apprentice)

demographics.occupation: Semi-retired finish carpenter (takes one or two small jobs a year through old contacts)
demographics.education: High school diploma plus completed Pacific Northwest Regional Council of Carpenters apprenticeship under Hal Greer

background.how_they_met: Both apprenticed under Hal Greer in southeast Portland in the late 1970s; started in overlapping cohorts and have stayed in close contact ever since.
background.why_close: Shared craft heritage, shared mentor (Hal), nearly five decades of summer-Saturday fishing on the Columbia, similar working-class trades background, mutual comfort with long silences. Ray is the friend Michael drinks an occasional bourbon with at home.

interests: fly fishing on the Columbia and Sandy
watching Westerns and Trail Blazers games
personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Short texts. Lowercase. Typos he doesn't fix. Maybe a thumbs-up emoji once a year. Heavy use of one-word replies — 'tomorrow?', 'roger', 'rain'. Sends photos of fish caught with no caption. Calls instead of texts for anything more than logistics.

shared_activities: Most summer Saturdays fishing for cutthroat trout on the Columbia
Occasional weeknight bourbon at Michael's house
Annual late-fall steelhead trip on the Sandy
Sporadic shop visits to consult on a tricky joinery problem
Trading old Hal-Greer-shop stories
recent_text_topics: Weather/water-level checks ahead of Saturday fishing — the Columbia's been high after April rain
Confirming who's bringing what (Ray brings the flies; Michael brings sandwiches and thermoses)
Brief, pointed exchanges about a political news headline they disagree on — usually one back-and-forth then dropped
Ray asking about Marcus's progress (he met Marcus once at the shop) and whether Michael needs a hand on the cabin
A photo of a 14-inch cutthroat Ray landed the week Michael missed due to his mother's appointment
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q7: 'There's Ray Mendoza — he was one of Hal Greer's apprentices same time as me, and we've stayed close almost fifty years. He lives in Troutdale, we fish together on the Columbia most summer Saturdays.' Q7 follow-up: 'We compare flies, complain about our knees, and watch the water.' Q24: 'Ray is more conservative than I am.' Q38: 'the occasional bourbon when Ray comes over.'

social_circle.name: Rachel Barron-Whitfield

demographics.occupation: Registered nurse, St. Charles Medical Center, Bend

background.how_they_met: Daughter; born ~1988 to Michael and Susan.
background.why_close: Adult parent-child bond strengthened by post-2020 conversations on race, by her postpartum-anxiety period after Ben in 2021, and by Michael's ~6-week visits to Bend. She's the politically progressive voice in the family who pushed Michael to read 'The Warmth of Other Suns,' and the one whose home Michael visits most regularly.

interests: hiking around Bend and Smith Rock
Episcopal worship at her small Bend parish
personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Mix of full-sentence updates and quick fragments around shift schedules. Uses emojis (heart, sun, the occasional 😂) and sends photos of the grandkids almost daily. Voice notes when she's on a walk. Comfortable texting heavy topics.

shared_activities: Hosting Michael and Susan in Bend every ~6 weeks
FaceTime calls with the grandkids
Book recommendations (she sends Michael titles; he reads them slowly)
Christmas-week and summer-week visits to Fairview
Drake Park Saturday-morning walks during Bend visits
social_circle.communication_frequency: daily (mix of short check-ins and grandkid photos)
recent_text_topics: Ben's pre-K teacher conference and a funny quote he gave the teacher about 'Grandpa's stool'
Asking Michael's read on a healthcare-staffing op-ed in the Oregonian
Coordinating dates for the next Bend visit — proposing a Friday in early June since Tom's parents are coming the following weekend
Eliza's ballet recital — sending a video clip; Michael responded with 'beautiful, kiddo'
Checking in on Grandma Marjorie after the recent medication change — nurse-to-family update on what to watch for
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q5: 'Rachel, our daughter, is thirty-seven, a registered nurse at St. Charles in Bend.' Q26: 'I had hard conversations with my daughter Rachel — she's more progressive than I am and she pushed me to read some things I wouldn't have picked up otherwise.' Q26 follow-up: 'The Warmth of Other Suns, by Isabel Wilkerson.' Q46: 'Rachel had postpartum anxiety after Ben, in 2021.' Q5 follow-up: 'We drive to Bend every six weeks or so.'

social_circle.name: Daniel Barron

demographics.occupation: Software developer at a healthcare company

background.how_they_met: Son; born ~1985 to Michael and Susan.
background.why_close: Adult parent-child bond, currently the family's logistical hub for Liam's visits to Fairview. Daniel is described by Michael as 'the steady one,' lower-volume than Rachel but reliably in touch. His Hillsboro proximity (~30 min) makes weekend visits routine.

interests: his son Liam's Lego builds and soccer
weekend home-improvement projects (calls Dad for advice)
personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Concise, polite, punctuated. Texts at predictable times (lunch, after Liam's bedtime). Sends links to Oregonian articles or YouTube woodworking videos without much commentary. Quietly funny once or twice a week.

shared_activities: Monthly Liam weekend visits to Fairview
Occasional Wednesday Lego-club pickups for Liam when Daniel is in a meeting jam
Phone calls/texts about home-repair questions at the Hillsboro house
Trail Blazers game-day banter
Liam's birthday and school events
recent_text_topics: Coordinating Liam's overnight in two weekends — asking if Grandpa wants help on a small workshop project
A question about how to seal a leaky exterior door threshold at the Hillsboro house
Forwarded YouTube link to a hand-cut dovetail video, with a 'thought you'd appreciate this'
Brief check-in after the Trail Blazers loss (text was just 'oof')
Confirming Christmas-week plans now that the Bend siblings have firmed up their dates
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q5: 'Our son Daniel is forty, lives in Hillsboro with his wife Beth, and they have a boy, Liam, who's nine. Daniel does software for a healthcare company.' Q11: 'Liam from Hillsboro maybe one weekend a month.' Q19 follow-up: 'When Daniel needs us, yes. Susan and I will drive over to Hillsboro for a Wednesday and get Liam from Lego club.' Q46: 'Daniel has always been the steady one.'

social_circle.name: Marcus Reyes

demographics.occupation: Carpentry apprentice (Pacific Northwest Regional Council of Carpenters); takes journey-level jobs through the local hall
demographics.education: High school diploma; active union apprenticeship program

background.how_they_met: Paired through the carpenters' local apprenticeship-program mentor match about two years ago after Marcus had been bouncing between gigs.
background.why_close: Saturday-afternoon shop sessions for two years; Michael describes the mentoring as 'a coping tool I didn't anticipate.' During the early-2025 hand flare, Marcus shifted to doing the cutting while Michael supervised, deepening the trust. Marcus has become a quasi-third-child figure Michael wants to see running his own shop by age 30.

key_traits: impatient by nature but learning to slow down
interests: carpentry and tools (TikTok and Instagram woodworkers)
Mexican-American food culture in east Multnomah County
personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Texts in lowercase, frequent shorthand ('thx', 'k', 'lol'), uses emojis liberally — 🔨🪵👍. Sends photos of his own job-site work for Michael's critique. Will occasionally voice-note when his hands are dirty. Calls Michael 'Mr. B' even in text.

shared_activities: Saturday-afternoon shop sessions (~2 PM onward)
Sourcing trips to local lumberyards and the occasional estate sale for old tools
Helping Michael on the back-cabin renovation in exchange for tool time
Apprenticeship-program events at the carpenters' local
Watching Timbers matches with a beer (non-alcoholic for Marcus on driving days)
recent_text_topics: A photo of a face-frame cabinet Marcus built solo on a side job, asking for honest feedback
Confirming Saturday's plan — Michael asked him to bring his own block plane this time
A question about whether to take a job with a kitchen contractor in Gresham or hold out for a finish-carpentry crew
Marcus checking in after hearing Michael's mother had a bad week — short, kind, 'thinking of you Mr. B'
Lining up an apprenticeship-graduation event in July that the carpenters' local is hosting
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q7: 'a younger fellow, Marcus, twenty-six, who I've been mentoring through the carpenters' local for about two years now. He comes by the shop Saturdays.' Q33 follow-up: 'The mentoring sessions with Marcus shifted to him doing the cutting and me supervising.' Q50: 'being useful to Marcus is a coping tool I didn't anticipate.' Q108: 'I'd like Marcus to be running his own shop by the time he's thirty.'
